authorization: User request to compare training-only state fitting with finite-class evaluation-time selection at matched information and resource budgets
prior_exposure: INF-001 v0.1 and v0.2 outcomes were known during design; this is not blinded or external preregistration
question: Which training-only selection rules reduce fitting error enough to avoid the multiplicity cost of finite-class evaluation selection, under common information, classes, world budgets and resource ceilings?

primary_contrast.comparison: posterior_risk minus evaluation_class probability of certifying summary level (or smaller)
primary_contrast.test: exact paired binomial/McNemar on discordant outcomes, two-sided alpha .05; one prespecified contrast; all other rates descriptive

method_roles.variance_penalized: secondary, training group-loss mean plus sqrt(2 V log(2 Q/.05)/T); tuning frozen; not a claimed training generalization certificate
method_roles.posterior_risk: primary training-only candidate: exact joint two-horizon Gaussian likelihood with shared offset and missing path integrated correctly, then posterior expected Brier-risk minimum within each unchanged finite class
method_roles.evaluation_class: primary comparison: class-minimum scalar EB at alpha/Q over frozen state members

generator: Exact inherited FiniteModel and WorldBatch.draw; four objects/world; both future labels supplied in training; same independent worlds and shared nuisance; original paths/priors/censoring/clock unchanged
matched_information: Every arm receives the same complete training batch including continuous outcomes at both horizons and the same model specification; ERM and variance penalty intentionally use the event indicators. All get the same pre-test library. Test labels can inform selection only for evaluation_class with its correction. No hidden-support, offset, or truth label can inform fitting.
library: Unmodified make_library: 9 / 70 / 131 nested entries. Same train-derived horizon-1 posterior mixtures available to all. New posterior-risk rule selects an existing member; does not add its joint-posterior mixture to the library.
fitting_targets: horizon-specific members; all-horizon adequacy, NOT a common recursive state
model_assumption: posterior-risk fitting assumes the registered generative family, observation law and noise; certificate validity only needs bounded iid-world losses and frozen predictors, but fitting power is not robust by assumption
test_budget: G = total_worlds - training_worlds. Every method in a cell uses identical T and G. Allocations are separate predeclared experiments, not selected after results.
coupling: For each case and replicate, a single 4096-world training pool and a separate 32704-world test pool supply nested prefixes across budgets. 300 primary independent pool pairs plus 100 control pairs. Comparisons across cells/arms are paired, not independent.
resource_matching: Common ceilings and exactly matched data/class budgets; actual costs are measured, NOT padded to equal time or claimed equal FLOPs. Numerical campaign reuses shared moments; isolated method benchmark reports unshared algorithmic costs.
fitting_failure_rule: Stop on invalid numerics, leakage, source mismatch or resource limit. An unresolved/negative scientific result is a valid outcome. No tuning or switches after evaluation.
operating_alarm: No minimum power gate. For each of 20 cells and 4 methods, binomial upper-tail check against .05 at family threshold .01/80. Gross-error check, not nominal size verification.
required_checks: test perturbation cannot change trained choices
reporting: certification fractions with pointwise exact binomial intervals
exact selected risk gaps and fitting regret by horizon
local_logbook: Entry only after tests, operating gates and clean-source numerical replay pass. Local experiment only, not live programme; no Git commands.
